i8283 p. 3 item 2.d; refused through gift.special. Over-refusal; the screen review's finding 0. BUG-0506.

i5329 p. 5, exception 13 (457 plan). A correctly coded 7 under 59½ draws Yes and retirement.screen_refused refuses. Over-refusal. BUG-0499.

unruled:retirement.combined_age#1.reason: Low: no rule for several survivor beneficiaries; vanishingly rare and partly covered by retirement.special.

s3.mfs refuses a married filing separately return.

unruled:sc.meals_80#1.reason: Changes value: employees' DOT duty meals are not asked for at 80%.

unruled:scveh.suv#1.reason: Low: the integral-enclosure condition is dropped; the vehicle it lets through is vanishingly rare.

unruled:tipjob.qualified#1.reason: Low: tokens are not named as cash, but a No refuses the employer's tips (tipjob.mixed).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 102, cash medium includes "tokens that are readily exchangeable for a fixed amount (for example, casino chips)". tipjob.qualified false makes tipjob.mixed true, which refuses tipjob.amount. Over-refusal. BUG-0511.

unruled:w2.box12_e#1.reason: No defect: USERRA make-up entries are refused.

findings.evidence: w2.box12_userra ("Does box 12 show an amount with a year after its code (make-up contributions for an earlier year under USERRA)?") refuses ("Form W-2 box 12 make-up contributions for an earlier year (USERRA)", iw2w3 p. 20).

unruled:carloan.col_ii_input#1.reason: No defect: Schedules E and F are refused, and column (ii) takes only the QPVLI part of the Schedule C interest.

findings.evidence: carloan.qpvli locator: "Schedules E and F are refused by scope.schedule1"; scope.schedule1 lists rental real estate (Schedule E) and farm income (Schedule F).

carloan.col_ii is zero unless carloan.eligible, else carloan.sc_allocated, which prorates the Schedule C interest by the qualifying part of the loan (sc_mixed_prorated, sc_refi; fr-2025-24154 p. 23, § 1.163-16(g)(1)). The full answer never reaches 22(ii) unreduced.

unruled:carloan.down#1.reason: Finding 0 changes value (a trade-in counted at its gross value as consideration besides its negative equity); finding 1 is a rare low.

findings.evidence: fr-2025-24154 § 1.163-16(d)(8): negative equity is the trade-in debt "to the extent such indebtedness exceeds the vehicle's trade-in value", so the trade-in value is already netted; (d)(2)(iii)(B) applies "any down payment (or other consideration provided by the taxpayer ...)" first against negative equity. The question's "or other consideration you provided" invites the gross trade-in value; carloan.nonqualifying_debt = nonqualifying - down (floor 0) then drops, raising carloan.mixed_qualifying and 22(iii). Trade-ins with negative equity are common.

Rebates applied at signing: the proposed regulation does not say whether a manufacturer rebate is consideration provided by the taxpayer; it only matters against nonqualifying amounts. Rare and unsettled.

unruled:carloan.financed#1.reason: No defect: each loan is its own roster entry, so 'this loan' is the new loan on a refinancing entry.

findings.evidence: Roster prompt ($carloan): "one entry per loan (a loan refinanced during 2025 is a separate entry)"; the refinancing entry is carloan.kind = refinanced and asks carloan.refi_balance separately. 'This loan when it was taken out' is the new loan's principal ($38,000 in Example 3).

unruled:carloan.interest#1.reason: No defect: the original and the refinancing loans are separate roster entries, each with its own 2025 interest.

findings.evidence: Roster prompt ($carloan): "one entry per loan (a loan refinanced during 2025 is a separate entry)". The original loan's 2025 interest is entered on its own entry (kind original, prorated by carloan.mixed_interest), so the new loan's ratio never cuts it.

unruled:carloan.kind#1.reason: Lows: an inherited loan later refinanced, and a second refinancing, fit the choices loosely; both rare.

findings.evidence: fr-2025-24154 § 1.163-16(d)(4) cap; on 'death' the tool takes the mixed path, where carloan.mixed/nonqualifying ask about "cash paid to you", so a cash-out is still excluded; only rolled-in fees escape. A 2025 loan inherited and refinanced within 2025 is vanishingly rare.

'Refinanced (this loan refinanced such a loan ...)' reads naturally to cover a chain, and carloan.refi_whole asks whether the refinanced loan "was not itself a refinancing for more than the balance it replaced", so the encoding expects chains. Wording only.

unruled:carloan.mixed#1.reason: No defect: carloan.mixed is read only on original and inherited loans; a refinancing is capped by refi_balance or refused.

findings.evidence: carloan.allocated takes carloan.refi_interest when kind = refinanced; carloan.mixed is read only through carloan.mixed_interest and carloan.sc_mixed, chosen for kind original or death. On a refinancing, carloan.refi_qualifying = smaller of refi_balance and financed, which already excludes rolled-in fees above the old balance (§ 1.163-16(d)(4)).

A refinancing of a partly qualifying loan is refused: carloan.refi_whole = no makes carloan.refi_nested true, which refuses carloan.refi_qualifying ("Refinancing of a loan that was itself only partly a qualifying vehicle loan").

unruled:carloan.nonqualifying#1.reason: Lows: the parenthetical names property, not services, and 'in the purchase' could take in items paid outside the loan.

findings.evidence: fr-2025-24154 § 1.163-16(d)(2)(ii), "property or services unrelated to an APV". The filer reached this question through carloan.mixed, whose first clause is "anything other than the vehicle and items customarily financed with it"; the general lead "amounts in the purchase that do not qualify" also covers it. A financed unrelated service is rare.

(d)(2)(ii) concerns indebtedness; the question follows carloan.mixed ("Did this loan also finance ..."), so 'in the purchase' reads as the financed amounts. A misreading lowers the deduction only for a filer who paid a nonqualifying item separately at the dealer. Wording.

unruled:carloan.refi_balance#1.reason: No defect: a refinancing of a partly qualifying loan is refused.

findings.evidence: carloan.refi_whole = no makes carloan.refi_nested true, which refuses carloan.refi_qualifying ("Refinancing of a loan that was itself only partly a qualifying vehicle loan"; § 1.163-16(d)(2)(iii) and (d)(4)). The honest-answer gap in refi_whole itself is ruled on carloan.refi_whole#1.

unruled:carloan.refi_whole#1.reason: Finding 0 changes value (refi_whole does not name the exclusions, so negative equity reads as customarily financed); findings 1 and 2 are lows.

findings.evidence: fr-2025-24154 § 1.163-16(d)(2)(ii): negative equity and collision or liability insurance are not customarily financed items "and as a result [are] not an SPVL"; preamble p. 20: "customarily financed ... determined on an industry-wide basis". carloan.mixed lists these exclusions; carloan.refi_whole says only "items customarily financed with it". A Yes keeps carloan.refi_nested false, and carloan.refi_qualifying = min(refi_balance, financed) counts the old loan's whole balance as SPVL, overstating 22(iii).

A three-loan chain inside 2025 (all loans must be originated after December 31, 2024) whose first loan was partly nonqualifying. The lead clause "Was all of the loan this loan refinanced a qualifying vehicle loan" covers it; only the parenthetical is incomplete. Vanishingly rare.
A No only refuses (carloan.refi_nested refuses carloan.refi_qualifying); the Yes reading is the right one for a whole-balance refinancing. Over-refusal.

unruled:carloan.requirements#1.reason: Finding 2 changes value (a refinancing loan was not 'used to buy the vehicle', so an honest No zeroes the deduction); findings 0 and 1 are rare lows.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 109 requirement 2, "The loan was originated by you". An assumed (not inherited) 2025 car loan is vanishingly rare, and carloan.kind offers no choice for it (original says "you took out this loan").

i1040gi p. 109, "If a loan met requirements 1 through 5 at the time it was originated by a previous obligor, and you became the obligor by reason of a previous obligor's death ...". The question tests "you expected"; an heir answers No and carloan.eligible is false (zero). The 'death' choice of carloan.kind says "the loan met the requirements when it was taken out" but this question does not. A 2025 loan whose obligor died in 2025 is vanishingly rare.

i1040gi p. 109, Refinanced loan, "interest paid on the refinanced amount is generally eligible ... so long as the new loan is secured by a first lien". The question's refinancing parenthetical covers only the origination date; "it was used to buy the vehicle" is literally false of a refinancing loan, and a No makes carloan.eligible false and 22(iii) zero on a supported path (kind = refinanced).

unruled:carloan.vehicle#1.reason: Low: an heir answers No to 'original use starting with you'; vanishingly rare.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 109, change in obligor by reason of death. The question requires original use "starting with you"; an heir answers No and carloan.eligible is false. Same defect as the death case in carloan.requirements; a 2025 loan whose obligor died in 2025 is vanishingly rare.

unruled:div.basis_reconciled#1.reason: Changes value: the question's wording lets a filer whose distribution exceeded basis answer Yes, which skips the refusal and omits the capital gain.

findings.evidence: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: "Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain." div.unsupported refuses only when box 3 > 0 and div.basis_reconciled_if_return_of_capital is false; no line reports the excess. A Yes from a filer whose distribution exceeded basis (basis reduced to zero) computes the return without the gain.

The same wording, "applied to records with no distribution exceeding basis", reads either as a scope limit (Yes) or as an assertion that none exceeded basis (No); the Yes reading omits the gain as in finding 0.

unruled:div.box12#1.reason: Finding 1 is covered by the nominee screen; finding 0 is a rare low.

Line 2a feeds the social security worksheet and modified AGI, so an omitted share changes those, but a co-owned muni fund paid in another's name with no nominee form is rare.

sb.unsupported ("Any nominee income ...") refuses sb.line6 (and lines 2 and 3) through sb.unsupported_if_income whenever interest, ordinary dividends or capital gain distributions are above zero; the pilot ruled the same for sb.ordinary_dividends#1. A fund paying only exempt-interest dividends to a nominee is the rare residue.

unruled:div.box2d#1.reason: No defect: nominee amounts are refused by sb.unsupported.

findings.evidence: div.box2d is asked only when box 2a > 0, which makes sb.has_income true; sb.unsupported ("Any nominee income ...") then refuses sb.line6 through sb.unsupported_if_income.

unruled:div.box3#1.reason: Finding 1 is covered by the nominee screen; finding 0 is a low (box 3 only screens).

sb.unsupported ("Any nominee income ...") refuses sb.line6 through sb.unsupported_if_income when ordinary dividends or capital gain distributions are above zero; a box 3 distribution with no box 1a or 2a is rare.

unruled:household.community_property#1.reason: No defect: the wide refusal is the owner's recorded reading for a married head of household in a community property state.

unruled:household.cp_married#1.reason: Findings 0 and 1 are refused by other questions; finding 2 only over-refuses.

findings.evidence: A widowed filer not filing jointly files single or head of household (married filing separately is refused, s3.mfs); household.spouse_died_2025 Yes makes household.widowed_2025 true, which refuses f1040.line12e.

unruled:household.married#1.reason: Lows: divorce-to-remarry only refuses; a 2025 widow(er) is refused as single or head of household, and Form 8889 tests marriage at year end.

unruled:household.spouse_died_2025#1.reason: Lows: a remarriage-and-divorce in 2025, an ex-spouse's death, and help that names only single and head of household; all rare or over-refusal.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 13, "Your spouse died in 2025 and you didn't remarry in 2025." A widow(er) who remarried and divorced again within 2025 gets a joint return with the deceased spouse; this does change the status, but is vanishingly rare.

unruled:household.unmarried#1.reason: Lows: divorce-to-remarry (vanishingly rare), civil unions (No only refuses), and a continuing prior-year nonresident-spouse election (rare).

p501 p. 6, Definition of marriage. i1040gi p. 14, a prior-year choice that "remains in effect". "You did not elect" is past tense and covers an earlier election for most readers; rare.

unruled:ira.special#1.reason: Low: deferred compensation in box 1 not shown in box 11 or code Z escapes the screen; rare and binds only when compensation limits the deduction.
